history.reason: Critical Windows portability failure: code uses os.OpenRoot() without build tags, will not compile on Windows. Violates acceptance criterion 10.3-10.4 requiring platform-specific isolation for Unix-only assertions.
history.retraction_reason: Invalid finding. os.OpenRoot() is cross-platform in Go 1.22+. Iteration 1 verdict was based on factual error about API portability. Verified with pinned Go 1.26.1 toolchain: cross-compilation succeeds, Windows tests pass, PE32+ executable builds.

history.reason: All acceptance criteria met. Implementation correctly hardens permissions, prevents TOCTOU races, isolates Unix tests with build tags, and builds cross-platform. Iteration 1 finding rescinded.
Unix existing-file ownership is not verified; attacker-owned regular files remain readable by their owner after chmod.
Windows runtime reports writable files as 0666 and cannot satisfy an exact 0600 post-Chmod check, so configured file logging fails.

Platform-specific secureLogFile implementations: Unix enforces ownership + mode hardening, Windows allows writable-open without POSIX assertions, other platforms no-op. Retains all common path safety validation.

Unix ownership validation fixed via build-tagged verifyLogFileOwner pre- and post-chmod checks. Windows helper correctly allows writable-0666 files without exact POSIX mode verification. Platform build tags prevent common code from bypassing safety. All acceptance criteria satisfied.
Final specialist re-review confirmed Unix ownership enforcement and Windows runtime behavior with no remaining high-confidence finding.
